title: Global pluripotential theory on hybrid spaces
author: Léonard Pille-Schneider
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 10 (2023), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.228
revision_note: Revised in place (no duplicate index created). Three inline keys (hyb-metric-dictionary, pure-fs-reduction, hybrid-bergman) were removed from independent_candidate_key because they are not recorded candidates in MATERIAL_RESULT.json; they are now null with the reason in the note, so that every non-null key in this file exists as a candidate. One note referring to a Fermat-family use was corrected: the Fermat/SYZ work is [PS22], cited in the introduction at line 205, and is not part of this paper's proofs.

numbering_basis.shared_counter: theo, prop, lem, cor and defn, ex, qu, rem are all declared with [equation], i.e. they share one counter with numbered equations of the class.
numbering_basis.independent_counter: thmA uses its own counter, printed as Alph via \thethmA=\Alph{thmA}; labels th:A and th:B.
numbering_basis.note: The shared-counter reset policy lives in the cedram class and could not be checked against the (unusable) reader.pdf, so no printed numbers are asserted.

results.label: th:A
results.statement: Theorem A (introduction form of theo psh hyb, forward direction only): for a polarized degeneration of complex manifolds and a psh metric phi with logarithmic growth at t=0, the singular metric phi^hyb with phi^hyb_0 = phi^NA and phi^hyb restricted to X_t equal to phi_t is plurisubharmonic.
results.disposition: author_stated_main_result_forward_half; full statement and proof at theo psh hyb (1163-1176, proof in sec proof psh)
results.note: Introduction form omits the converse; count the main result once, at the body statement.

results.label: theo Favre intro
results.statement: Quoted result of Favre [Fav, Th. 4.2]: for a projective degeneration polarized by an ample L and continuous psh phi on (X^hyb, L^hyb), the family of Monge-Ampere measures mu_t = MA(phi_t) is weakly continuous.

results.label: th:B
results.statement: Theorem B (introduction form of THEO KE NEG): for a degeneration of canonically polarized manifolds with semistable reduction, the metric with phi|X = phi_KE and phi_0 = phi_{K_{X_c/R}} is continuous and psh.
results.disposition: author_stated_main_result_forward_half; full statement at THEO KE NEG 1508-1514

results.statement: Definition: submultiplicative semi-norm, norm, Banach ring.
Definition: Berkovich spectrum M(A) and the map q to Spec(A).
Example: M(Z) as an infinite wedge of segments (Ostrowski).

results.label: def an
results.statement: Definition: analytification Y^an of an affine finite-type A-algebra, glued for X of finite type.

results.label: ex GM
results.statement: Example: over C with the Euclidean absolute value, Y^an = Y(C) with the Euclidean topology (Gelfand-Mazur).
Example: for a complete non-Archimedean K, points of X^an are pairs (scheme point, real valuation on the residue function field); support map.
Definition: residue field H(x) of M(A) at x.

results.label: prop gbr
results.statement: Proposition: the fiber of X^an over x is canonically homeomorphic to the analytification of X_{H(x)}, and the base change map is the inclusion.
results.note: Two-paragraph affine reduction plus gluing; standard functoriality of analytification. Not an advanced core.

results.statement: Remark: for geometric base rings in the sense of Lemanissier-Poineau, X^an_B is the fiber product; all Banach rings in the paper are of this kind.

results.label: def Mbir
results.statement: Definition: Zariski-dense points of M(A) and the subset M(A)^eta.
Definition: model of X over R, special fiber, group Div_0 of vertical Weil divisors.

results.label: def dual cpx
results.statement: Definition: dual complex D(X_0) of an snc model via simplices tau_Y and incidence.
Definition: divisorial valuations X^div, dense in X^an.

results.label: prop casi mono
results.statement: Quasi-monomial valuation existence and uniqueness, attributed to [MN, Prop. 2.4.4].
Definition: skeleton Sk(X) as the image of D(X_0).
Definition: Berkovich retraction rho_X; strong deformation retraction attributed to Berkovich.
Lemma: for a vertical ideal sheaf I on a model, phi_I restricted to any snc skeleton is integral piecewise-affine; the converse is asserted in the following prose.
results.note: Stated inline after 'This implies for instance the following'; no proof given. Recorded as an author-unproved inline claim.

results.label: def model f
results.statement: Definition: integral piecewise-affine (Z-PA) function.
Definition: hybrid Banach ring k^hyb with norm max(1,|z|).

results.label: cercle hyb
results.statement: Lemma [BJ, Prop. A.4]: tau from the closed disk of radius r to M(A_r) is a homeomorphism, with |f|_t = r^{ord_0 f} at t=0 and r^{log|f(t)|/log|t|} otherwise.
Definition: hybrid space X^hyb_r as the analytification of X_{A_r} over A_r, with structure map to C^hyb(r).

results.label: topo hyb
results.statement: Proposition [Fav, Th. 1.2]: fiber at 0 identified with X^an; homeomorphism beta from the punctured disk onto the complement of the zero fiber, compatible with projections, with |phi(beta(z))| = |phi(z)|^{log r/log|t|}. LITERAL SOURCE POINT on the exponent, see SCOPE_BOUNDARIES.

results.label: prop bc hyb
results.statement: Proposition: base-change diagram from C^hyb to A_r; F restricted to the zero fiber is f and on nonzero fibers induces the identity on X^hol under the homeomorphisms of Section 1.3.
results.note: Called a 'straightforward consequence of transitivity of base change'; no proof.

results.statement: Definition: continuous metric on L^an via local trivializing sections.
Example: A = C recovers Hermitian metrics.
Example: the trivial metric over a trivially-valued field.
Example: tropical Fubini-Study metric on O(1) over P^N_A; note the author calls it the tropical FS metric precisely because it is not the usual one when A = C.
Definition: singular metric (usc local potentials, not identically -infinity).
Example: the metric m^{-1}log|s_0| attached to a global section of L^m, singular along its zero locus.
Definition: pullback metric f^*phi.
Example: base change to H(x) equals restriction to the fiber.

results.label: theo berg exp
results.statement: [BE, Th. 7.1] (after Demailly): any psh metric on a semi-ample L over a complex projective variety is a decreasing pointwise limit of Fubini-Study metrics.
Definition: semi-positive singular metric over a non-Archimedean field as a pointwise decreasing limit of tropical Fubini-Study metrics.

results.label: theo psh1
results.statement: Theorem: over a complex projective variety with semi-ample L, every psh metric is a decreasing limit of a net of tropical Fubini-Study metrics.
results.note: Proof (610-618) turns a squared-sum FS metric into a max via chi(x)=1/(2m)log(sum e^{2mx}), invokes the later Lemma prop homo, then [BE, Th. 7.1]. Mechanism inherited; no new core.

results.label: ex model
results.statement: Example: model metrics on a normal projective R-model, the sup-norm unit-ball property, and identification with pure FS metrics and their differences via [BE, Th. 5.14].
Definition: tropical Fubini-Study metric max_j(log|s_j|+a_j)/m on a finite-type A-scheme; FS^tau(L), FS^tau(X), pure FS.

results.label: prop.FS
results.statement: Proposition: FS^tau(L) is closed under constants, max, sums over different L_i, division by m, rational convex combinations, pullback and base change.
results.note: Called straightforward consequences of the definition; no proof. Used as an input elsewhere.

results.statement: Definition: DFS (difference of Fubini-Study) metrics and DFS functions.
Theorem: for X/A projective, the Q-vector space DFS(X) is dense in C^0(X^an).
results.note: Proof (671-695): Stone-Weierstrass after checking Q-vector space/max/constants, then point separation on P^n_A; said to be 'essentially the same proof as [BJtriv, Th. 2.7]'. Not a new core.

results.statement: Example: FS functions on M(A) and their pullback along X^an -> M(A).

Main definition: PSH(X,L) is the class of singular metrics that are pointwise decreasing limits of nets of tropical FS metrics and whose fiber restrictions phi_x are not identically -infinity for all Zariski-dense x in M(A).
results.note: The paper's global definition; a definition carries no proof obligation and is not itself a candidate.

results.statement: Definition: CPSH(X,L), continuous psh metrics with the uniform-convergence topology.

results.label: prop psh
results.statement: Proposition: PSH closed under constants, sums, max, division by m, real convex combinations, decreasing limits subject to the non--infinity condition, and uniform limits when X/A is proper.
results.note: Proof at 734 attributes items 1-5 to prop.FS and items 6-7 to [BJtriv, Lem. 4.6]. No new mechanism.

results.statement: [BJtriv, Prop. 5.20]: for X/A proper, phi is in CPSH iff it is a uniform limit of a net in FS^tau.

results.label: ex fs sing
results.statement: Example: m^{-1}log|s| is in PSH as a decreasing limit of explicit FS metrics; finite maxima of the log|s_alpha| are psh; the fiber at a Zariski-dense point is finite by flatness.
Remark: PSH is not stable under non-flat base change and a psh metric may become identically -infinity; the author deliberately excludes such metrics.
results.note: Scope boundary: later statements inherit the non--infinity condition on Zariski-dense fibers.

results.label: theo psh2
results.statement: Theorem: for complex projective X and semi-ample L, PSH(X,L) as defined here coincides with the usual class of psh metrics.
results.note: Declared a mere reformulation of theo psh1; no separate proof.

results.statement: Proposition: order-preserving injective maps rho_r: PSH(C^hyb(r)) -> SH(D_r)+R log|t| and rho_{r',r}: SH(D_{r'})+R log|t| -> PSH(C^hyb(r)) for r'>r, with phi(0)=log r * nu_0(rho_r(phi)) for continuous phi and tilde phi(0)=nu_0(phi)/log r, and rho_r o rho_{r',r} equal to restriction up to scaling.
results.note: Forward map and Lelong formulas proved for FS^tau and then by decreasing limits (803-820); the converse (821) is explicitly reduced to the later Theorem theo psh hyb; the composition claim (823) is 'clear from the constructions'. The sentence at 825 about the image on CPSH is an explicit expectation, not a theorem. Candidate is below the advanced band for exactly these reasons.

results.statement: Remark: the function equal to 1 at 0 and 0 elsewhere on C^hyb(r) is psh, illustrating that 0 is non-pluripolar and that Lelong numbers jump along max(log|t|,-j).

Proposition: continuous psh functions on M(Z) are exactly those whose branch restrictions are convex with the stated sign conditions on the outgoing slopes and whose slope sum at 0 is nonnegative; equivalently subharmonic on the R-tree. Consequence at 845: a point is polar iff it is the outer end of a p-adic branch.
results.note: Proof 846-904: FS slope computation via gcd/lcm of maximizers, then four construction steps; the Step-3 eps_k correction is the non-obvious part. The consequence at 845 is asserted, not separately proved.

results.statement: Definition: hybrid (continuous) metric on L, and PSH(L^hyb).

results.label: prop metric hyb
results.statement: Proposition: a continuous hybrid metric is equivalent to a continuous family (phi_t) on the L_t for t in the punctured closed disk together with a continuous phi_0 on L^an, subject to log||s||_{phi_t}/log_r|t| extending continuously by log||s||_{phi_0}; the data is unique.
results.note: Proof 926-945 uses beta_t, beta_0 and the rescaling exponent. Recorded as context, not as a candidate: it is the dictionary through which every later statement is phrased, and it contains no estimate.

results.statement: Example: for a global section s of mL, m^{-1}log|s| restricts on nonzero fibers to m^{-1}log|s_t|, and with a constant c to m^{-1}(log|s| + c log_r|t|).

results.label: rem pure
results.statement: Remark: over a hybrid ring, c/log r with c rational equals log|f| for some f in A_r, so any psh hybrid metric is a decreasing limit of PURE Fubini-Study metrics; this fails for a general Banach ring such as Z.
results.note: Supporting device with an explicit computation (rational approximation of c, absorb into t^{c_j}s). It is used inside the main theorem's Fubini-Study reduction and inside the admissible-data dictionary at 1496; it is the same 'constants come from log|f| over a hybrid ring' observation, so it is not counted as a separate candidate.

results.label: prop homo sing
results.statement: Proposition: the hybrid Bergman metric of a finite family of global sections of mL (squared sum on nonzero fibers, max at the zero fiber) is semi-positive.
results.note: Proof 990-999 basepoint-frees mL, augments the family with constants b_{alpha,j}=0 or -j, and applies Lemma prop homo. A component of the main mechanism; counted under jep228-convex-to-max-transfer, not separately.

results.label: prop homo
results.statement: Lemma: for a convex chi on R^N with chi(x+c1)=chi(x)+c and chi - max bounded, the hybrid metric with phi_{chi,t}=chi(phi_{1,t},...,phi_{N,t}) on nonzero fibers and max_i log|s_i| at the zero fiber is continuous semi-positive; the key transfer between Archimedean convex combinations and the non-Archimedean maximum.
results.note: Proof 1018-1049: continuity via |eps(t)| <= C/log_r|t| from the boundedness of chi - max; semi-positivity via decreasing piecewise-affine chi_j with rational slopes u_alpha in the simplex and Conv(u_alpha)=sigma (input from [PS22, Prop. 2.6]) so that max_alpha <u_alpha,x> = max(x).

results.label: ex homo
results.statement: Example: on P^N x D^* with the standard polarization, gluing the Euclidean FS metric on fibers with the non-Archimedean FS metric at 0 is continuous semi-positive and is not itself a FS metric.
Example: Hermitian norms on H^0(X,mL), apartments, geodesic rays, the non-Archimedean norm gamma^NA, and the hybrid Bergman metric phi_lambda of a geodesic ray, continuous and psh by prop homo.

results.label: def log g
results.statement: Definition [Reb, Lem. 2.3.2]: logarithmic growth at t=0, in three equivalent forms.

results.label: theo ext phina
results.statement: [BBJ, Th. 6.2; Reb, Th. 3.3.1]: the generic-Lelong-number function psi^NA on divisorial valuations has a unique lsc extension to X^an and phi^NA = phi_L + psi^NA is semi-positive.
results.note: The construction at 1117-1129 (v_E, b_E, nu_E, psi^NA(v)=log r/b_E * nu_E) is exposition of cited results, not a new proof.

results.label: ex bdd model
results.statement: Example: if phi is locally bounded and extends psh on a nef model then psi^NA=0 and phi^NA is the model metric.

results.label: ex Lelong TFS
results.statement: Example: for a tropical FS metric with sections extending to a model, nu_E(phi)=(phi_0-phi_L)(v_E), so psi^NA=phi_0-phi_L and phi^NA is the restriction to X^an.
results.note: Used inside the main theorem's proof and in prop semic phina (via phi_j^0=phi_j^NA). Source-notation points at 1146 and 1158 recorded separately.

results.label: theo psh hyb
results.statement: Main Theorem (full statement): for a polarized degeneration of complex polarized varieties over D^* and phi in PSH(X,L) with logarithmic growth at 0, phi^hyb with phi^hyb|X_t=phi_t and phi^hyb_0=phi^NA is semi-positive; conversely any phi^hyb in CPSH(X^hyb,L^hyb) restricts, after shrinking to radius r-eps, to a psh metric on the punctured restriction with logarithmic growth at 0 and with phi^NA=phi^hyb_0.
results.note: Proof split into: multiplier-ideal Bergman reduction (1237-1240, technical work referred to the appendix), prop sum psh (1261-1287), decreasing limits (1289), partial converse (1291-1295), continuity of (.)^NA (lemma 1298-1307), and a density identification (1308-1312). Full proof only modulo the appendix theorem theo reg psh.

results.label: prop semic phina
results.statement: Proposition: for phi in PSH(L^hyb), phi_0 >= phi_NA on X^an; conversely for phi in E^1(L) fiberwise finite energy and any psi in E^1(L^an) with psi >= phi^NA there is a psh extension tilde phi in E^1(L^hyb) with tilde phi_0=psi.
results.note: Proof 1190-1202: first part by decreasing nets and semicontinuity of Lelong numbers on divisorial points; second part by eta_j = max(psi^hyb, phi^hyb - j log|e|) and a decreasing limit, citing [Reb] and Theorem theo psh hyb. External energy inputs: E^1, Darvas metric, relative maximality [Klim]. Component of the main mechanism; not counted separately.

results.statement: Example: maximal degenerations of abelian varieties; cubic metrics are psh with logarithmic growth and the hybrid metric is continuous by [GO, Th. 4.13], with phi^NA computed in [Liu].

results.label: prop psh cont
results.statement: Proposition: if phi in PSH(X,L) extends as a CONTINUOUS metric on L^hyb, then the extension is semi-positive.
results.note: Proof 1208-1213 uses the lemma at 1214-1223, agreement on rational points of skeletons and [BFJ2, Prop. 7.6]. Makes the KE application possible.

results.statement: Lemma: for phi psh with logarithmic growth and a divisorial valuation v_E determined on an snc model on which phi extends psh, there is a sequence z_j in X converging to v_E in X^hyb with (phi-phi_0)(z_j)/log_r|t| -> psi^NA(v_E).
results.note: Proof uses a very general point of E not on other components and the hybrid convergence of z_j to v_E ([BJ, Def. 2.3]). The device inside jep228-continuous-sufficiency.

results.statement: Question (taken from [Fav, Quest. 1]): if phi is continuous semi-positive and phi^NA is continuous, is phi^hyb continuous psh? Prose at 1229-1233 says it reduces to a t-independent bound phi_m - phi <= eps_m |log|t||^{-1}.
results.note: Register as a question only.

results.label: prop sum psh
results.statement: Proposition: for every m>0 the hybrid metric built from multiplier-ideal Bergman data is semi-positive.
results.note: Proof 1270-1287: truncate the Hilbert basis, apply prop homo sing, get uniform convergence on X_{r+eps} via prop som part and on X^an via stability of J_q=I_m plus Dini. Component of the main theorem's proof.

results.statement: Lemma: the map (.)^NA: CPSH(L^hyb) -> CPSH(L^an) is well defined and continuous for uniform convergence.
results.note: Proof: order preservation [Reb, Th. 3.3.1], translation equivariance, uniform limits along FS^tau nets.

results.statement: Definition: psh ray (S^1-invariant psh metric on X x D^*).
[BBJ, Th. 6.2] in isotrivial form: psi^NA extends continuously and phi^NA=psi^NA+phi^triv is psh; prose at 1346 says it is 'essentially a special case of Theorem theo ext phina'.
Proposition: for r in (0,1) the metric with phi^hyb_0=phi^NA and phi^hyb|X_lambda = lambda phi_{1/lambda} is semi-positive on X^hyb_0, and Phi^hyb = F^* phi^hyb.
results.note: The equality is 'straightforward'; positivity is obtained by redoing the main proof with S^1-equivariant Hilbert bases, and the author says 'we omit the details' (1359). Omitted-detail adaptation of the main mechanism, hence a recorded gap rather than a separate core.

results.label: ex MA model
results.statement: [CL] explicit MA measure of nef model metrics as sum_E b_E (L_1...L_n . E) delta_{v_E}.
[BE, Prop. 8.3]: symmetry/multilinearity, positivity on FS tuples, total mass, and the integration-by-parts identity.
[BE, Th. 8.4]: unique extension of the MA operator to continuous psh metrics over a complete valued field, continuous for uniform convergence and weak convergence of measures.
Remark: E^1 is defined over any non-Archimedean field but the MA operator on E^1 is known only in the discretely-valued char 0 case [BFJ2] and the trivially-valued case [BJv4].
Remark: Chambert-Loir-Ducros curvature currents; [CLD, Th. 6.9.3] agreement with the mixed MA measure for psh model metrics.
[Y] Yau's solution of the Calabi conjecture.

results.label: theo sol MA
results.statement: [BFJ1, Th. A; BGJKM]: unique continuous psh solution of MA(phi)=mu for a probability measure supported on an snc skeleton over a discretely valued equicharacteristic-zero field.
Definition: the family of Monge-Ampere measures of a tuple of continuous psh metrics as the pushforward of the fiberwise MA measures to X^an.
Question: for flat projective X/A and continuous psh phi_i, is x -> int psi (MA(phi))_x continuous on M(A)? Flatness (1441-1445) is needed for the fiberwise total mass to be independent of x.

results.label: lem CLN
results.statement: [BE, Lem. 8.6] Chern-Levine-Nirenberg estimate for mixed MA pairings.

results.label: theo cont MA
results.statement: Theorem: for a smooth degeneration relatively polarized by an ample L and phi in CPSH(X^hyb,L^hyb), the MA measures are weakly continuous: int_{X_t} f (dd^c phi_t)^n -> int_{X^an} f MA(phi_0) for every continuous f.
results.note: Continuity itself is [Fav, Th. 4.2] and is not reproved; the author proves instead (1465-1496) that Favre's admissible-data model functions coincide with pure hybrid FS metrics. External in substance; candidate is below the advanced band.

results.label: THEO KE NEG
results.statement: Theorem: for a degeneration of canonically polarized manifolds with semistable reduction and phi_KE the KE family, the hybrid metric with phi|X=phi_KE and phi_0=phi_{K_{X_c/R}} is continuous and semi-positive.
results.note: Proof reduces via prop psh cont to continuity, subtracts the hybrid FS reference metric whose zero fiber is the canonical model metric, and reduces to |psi_t/log|t|| -> 0, an 'easy consequence' of [Song, Cor. 4.1, Lem. 4.2]. Analytic input external; proof ends with an explicit qed. Candidate is below the advanced band.

results.statement: Corollary: mu_t = omega_t^n converge weakly on X^hyb to mu_0 = MA(phi_{K_{X_c}}), explicitly sum_i b_i ((K_{X_c})^n . D_i) delta_{v_i}.
results.note: No separate proof; immediate from theo cont MA plus the explicit model formula. Line 1528 notes a direct prior proof in [PS, Th. A].

results.statement: [BCHM; KNX] existence and uniqueness (after finite base change) of the canonical model with canonical total space, slc reduced central fiber, relatively ample relative canonical.
Remark: the natural map from any semistable model to the canonical model is a rational contraction.

[Song, Th. 1.1]: existence and uniqueness of a KE current on the slc central fiber, smooth on the regular locus, locally bounded on the log terminal locus, with no mass on the singularities and total mass [K_{X_{c,0}}]^n.
Remark: the current matches [BG] by uniqueness, and int_{D_i} omega_KE^n = (K_{X_c}^n . D_i) via the conductor and the projection formula.

results.label: prop Song
results.statement: [Song, Cor. 4.1, Lem. 4.2]: uniform upper bound sup_{X_t} psi_t <= C and, for eps>0, psi_t >= eps(sum_{i != i_0} phi_i + sum_{j in J'} psi_j) - C_eps; plus smooth convergence away from the singular locus under the stated hypotheses.
results.note: The author notes a small abuse: the right-hand side is a metric, not a function.

results.statement: Remark: pointed Gromov-Hausdorff consequences; higher-dimensional bases via [SSW]; the collapsing region via [Zh] under semistability.
Definition: multiplier ideal sheaf I(phi).

results.label: def ansing
results.statement: Definition: analytic singularities along a coherent ideal sheaf J.

results.label: theo reg psh
results.statement: Theorem (appendix main result): for smooth Kaehler Y admitting a proper holomorphic map to a bounded open subset of C, a relatively ample L and phi in PSH(Y,L), for every relatively compact Y' there is a sequence phi_j in PSH(Y',L) decreasing pointwise to phi on Y' with 2^j phi_j having analytic singularities of the form I_{2^j}.
results.note: Structure: prop glob gen, Hilbert-space Bergman metrics, prop som part for analytic singularities, two-sided pointwise bounds via subharmonicity and Ohsawa-Takegoshi, almost subadditivity via OT on the diagonal, and the decreasing sequence phi_j = phi_{2^j-m_0,m_0}+2^{-j-2}C. Author states the precise statement was not found in the literature; mechanism largely classical.

results.label: prop glob gen
results.statement: Proposition: for Y' relatively compact in Y_c there is m_0 such that O_Y((m+m_0)L tensor I_m) is generated by global sections on Y_c for all m>=1.
results.note: Proof: make m_0 L - K_Y - nH relatively ample, apply the relative Castelnuovo-Mumford criterion [DEL, Lem. 1.4] and Nadel vanishing [Nad]/[BFJ2, Th. B.8]; argument from [BBJ, Lem. 5.6]. Sub-result, not separately counted.

results.label: prop som part
results.statement: Proposition: the partial-sum Bergman metrics phi_{m,m_0,q} converge uniformly to phi_{m,m_0} over Y' and phi_{m,m_0} has analytic singularities of the form I_m over Y'.
results.note: Proof 1707-1742: compare F_q and F via the two-variable coherent ideal generated by s_l(z)conj(s_l(w)), strong Noetherian property and Dini; adapted from [DPS, Th. 2.2.1, step 2]. Sub-result, not separately counted.

unproved_claims_and_open_items.content: The Z-PA restriction lemma and its converse are stated without proof.
The image of rho_r on CPSH is EXPECTED to be the continuous subharmonic functions on the punctured disk with finite Lelong number at 0: stated as an expectation, not a theorem.
Favre's Question 1 on continuity of phi^hyb when phi^NA is continuous; the needed uniform estimate is said to be difficult.
Question on weak continuity of the fiberwise MA family over a general integral Banach ring.
